description.summary: A creature with legs shorter on one side than the other, allowing it to walk comfortably on steep hillsides but only in one direction.
description.full: The Sidehill Gouger is a fearsome critter from American lumberjack folklore, distinguished by having legs shorter on one side of its body than the other. This asymmetry allows it to walk perfectly on steep hillsides, but only in one direction around the hill. According to the tales, different species exist for clockwise versus counterclockwise travel, and a Sidehill Gouger is fatally vulnerable if caught on the wrong side of a hill. The creature represents the peak of fearsome critter absurdity - an obviously impossible anatomy presented as a humorous 'explanation' for adaptation to mountainous terrain. It was purely for entertainment, never meant to be believed.
